items.heading: Bels fight for third place at Sportcity
items.summary: Report and results of British Athletics League Premiership match two at Manchester Sportcity, where Belgrave took third place by one point and climbed out of the relegation zone.
items.text:
British Athletics League Premiership

Match Two, Manchester Sportcity, 2 June 2007.

Bels fight for third place at Sportcity

Bill Laws reports:- Let’s start with a few statistics. In match 1 we did not contest 99 points and in the whole match 139 points were unused. So between them the remaining seven clubs passed on 40 points or roughly six points per club. No wonder we struggled. Determined to rectify the situation the team managers dug deep and contacted every athlete who had competed for Belgrave over the past three years. Many had slipped under the radar so the task was daunting especially as match 2 of the Premiership was only five days after the European Clubs Cup in Portugal and the team managers were “creamed”. If salaried, they would have earned their crust this week. As it was, the joy of leading one of the best club teams in the country had to suffice.

With UKA calling up our top athletes for the Glasgow Grand Prix and the BMC meetings demanding the attention of our middle distance men, the task was harder than ever, but eventually a team of 26 was assembled in Manchester for one of the most fiercely contested matches anyone could remember. Every point was going to count but the outcome was always going to be in doubt until the last event. Of the 22 Belgravians who lined up for match 1 only 10 made it for this one. So 16 freshers were there to scrap for every point.

The start was not good

The start was not good. Matt Douglas had reported sick the day before and was in bed when the A 400H started. Pensioner Paul Beaumont again filled in for the points but even he was injured so ignore the time. Ryan Dinham, recovering from surgery, may be out for the rest of the season so the long hurdles continues to be a disaster. In the pole vault Keith Higham had just one clearance - fortunately that was at 5.00m to win the B – and Joe Ive cleared 5.20m to get second in the A on count back. Looking better!

Meanwhile the discus boys were in the coach ready to transfer to another stadium for their competition. The outside throwing area at Manchester has a slope that would make a mountain goat feel at home. Unsuitable for record purposes, it is a disgrace for a stadium purporting to be the leading venue in the UK. As a result several of the top throwers had stayed away and both Scot Thompson and Mark Allen gained good points despite below par performances into a tricky head wind. Mark later threw a pb in the shot for bronze in the A while Scot won the B event with his last effort. In the hammer Mick Jones improved his season’s best by 4m to gain second spot and he was one happy bunny. More excellent points had come from our throwers then, exceeding our predictions.

Good points in the sprint hurdles

Now back to the track where the 100m was disappointing, with Darren Chin’s blocks slipping and Jason Hussain looking as though he had just got out of bed. Fortunately they reacted positively and both gained second places in the 200m to make amends. In the A 200m Andy Turner’s winning time was good enough to win “man of the match” so Darren’s performance was exceptional. It was great to see Paskar Owor back for the 800m and he didn’t disappoint with a close second place; then to Neil Speaight who despite a cold also gained silver in the B with a time faster than the winner of the A. More good points came in the sprint hurdles where William Sharman ran a season’s best for second followed by an unexpected victory by Kevin Sempers in the B. Kevin had an awful start and only got his chest in front on the line. It looks as though his pb in this event may well be revised in next week’s Decathlon championships. The 400m brought us back to earth as Gavin Selway struggled for last spot in the A while Ryan Thomas ran a similar time for third in the B.

13 points from the 'chasers

Back from his gruelling 5000m in the “Euroclubs” Simon Jones produced a pb to gain third spot in the A but Peter Willis in the B race struggled throughout, possibly due to racing in a BMC meet a couple of days earlier. New men in the steeplechase produced 13 points where recently we have had only 5. Sam Aldridge claimed he had only started training after match 1 so his fourth spot was a big bonus. David Mason gained sixth spot in the B chase and then agreed to début in the TJ. One point perhaps but he was only a tantalising 13cm off sixth spot. Gary Wilson jumped a 14.51m pb in zero wind and there is plenty more to come from him. In the long jump Adrian Phillips broke 7m for the first time but could only finish fifth in a competition where seven men cleared seven metres. There was some confusion, as Newham & Essex Beagles seemed to have three competitors. All became clear when Chris Tomlinson explained he had been due to compete in Greece but had been turned round at the airport because his passport was damaged and therefore not valid. An 8.10m windy effort from him meant the weekend wasn’t wasted. Louis Evling-Jones was disappointed with his 6.87m effort but he secured fourth spot in the B event.

Back to the track for the 1500m where Neil Speaight had agreed to double. His cold seemed to be getting the upper hand as he struggled to maintain contact with the leading group of ten but just as we were despairing he started to close the gap – but there was only 300m left! The task seemed impossible but fortunately Neil didn’t appear to think so and a really fast last 200m saw him cruise into third spot while Alex Bodin gained more valuable experience in the B race.

Third spot - just!

So as the meeting moved towards its conclusion the points scores were announced. Still holding fourth spot we remembered earlier visits to Manchester where the last four events had seen Belgrave drift down the results table. This time there was no such capitulation. Excellent points came in the high jump with Darvin Edwards winning the A event on count back as three men cleared 2.15m, and Kevin Sempers added more by finishing second in the B with a season’s best of 2.00m. While the javelin was taking an age the relays demanded our attention. Three recognised sprinters got the baton round in fine form to Kevin Sempers, fresh from the high jump. Safety first was the order of the day and the baton crossed the line in sixth spot – job done. Then to the long relay where AAA’s decathlon champion Louis Evling-Jones joined the specialist one lappers including Set Osho – making his first outing of the year following back problems. Ryan Thomas, Louis and Gavin Selway made sure we remained in contention at the final handover. Our closest rivals in the points table, Sheffield, had Richard Buck on the last leg, which was bound to be tasty. How would Set fare? - unbelievably well. With an official split of 46.9 he held on for an excellent third place and proved he is well and truly back. So with just the javelin result to come in we were in third spot just five points ahead of Sheffield. Eventually the javelin result was announced – Lee Doran of Sheffield had won the A (16 points) but Tom Dobbing had held on to fourth (10 points). Ouch! Then the B results: Wes Smith was second (10 points) with Sam Ellis of Sheffield third (8 points). Yes!!! Up went the cheers. Third spot by just one point. Each and every team member had fought for this. We are out of the relegation zone but can be assured that the next two matches are going to be real scraps. Suddenly the BAL Premiership seems an exciting place to be.

items.heading: Opposition a bit tasty in Albufeira
items.summary: Report and results of the European Champion Clubs Cup Group A in Albufeira, where Belgrave finished seventh and were relegated to Group B.
items.text:
European Champion Clubs Cup Group A
Albufeira, Portugal, 26-27 May 2007.

Opposition a bit tasty in Albufeira

Bill Laws writes:- Belgrave’s 9th incursion into Europe for the men’s Champion Clubs Cup turned out to be more traumatic than any of the preceding fixtures. Travel problems played some part in a generally lack lustre overall performance and several athletes who were opening their season paid the price for lack of earlier competition. Only peak performances had much hope of producing good points when virtually every event had a sprinkling of Olympic finalists.

The team had travelled out on two flights. The first was early and meant the team mustering at 4.30 am while the second afternoon flight was delayed six hours resulting in part of the team arriving at Faro Airport after midnight and arriving in Albufeira at 1.30am on the first day of competition. Such are the joys of travelling on a Bank Holiday weekend.

The local weather conditions for the first day of competition were warm but windy with headwinds down the home straight of up to 3.7m/s. The sprint times suffered accordingly and the longer races became tactical with results being decided by the fast finishers. At this level there are some really quick men in the track races and it was a lesson to all to see how some of our men who prided themselves on being a bit tasty were blown away by the awesome finishing speed of the other team’s athletes.

Our two wins were on the track with William Sharman getting the photo decision following an apparent dead heat with Moscow’s Borisov. Later William led off our victorious sprint relay squad. Chris Lambert went off fractionally early, checked but took the baton in zone. Darren Chin timed the next handover to perfection and Wade Bennett Jackson entered the home straight with a clear lead. Easing over the last ten metres and looking left he was almost run down by the fast finishing Russian, Yepishin, who was on his right and had earlier finished third in the 100 to Wade’s fifth placing. Still a win is a win and the squad celebrated accordingly.

We had predicted 35 points on day one and ended on 34 with just 6 points covering the bottom four teams. We then predicted 38 points on day two which, if achieved, would have taken us halfway up the table. But as events unfolded we managed to glean only 22 more precious points and finished up in the relegation spot to Group B.

There were some notable achievements including three pb’s. Chris Gearing finished the shot with a new best of 17.90m to gain an excellent fourth place in exalted company. Neil Speaight ran a lifetime best in the 3000m the day after finishing fourth in the 1500m in which local hero, sprint specialist and Olympic bronze medallist Rui Silva could only manage second. And finally triple jumper novice Gary Wilson leapt a windy 14.57m competing for the first time off the 13m board. So a big day for him with lots more to come.

The positives we take from this are that a number of very young athletes gained experience at the highest level. They all came through it well, and have been inspired to move on to greater things. We wish them well.

On the negative side we were disappointed to see other teams with full quotas of high scoring foreign athletes. One team had signed a South African athlete 10 days earlier and had got over the rules by making him a citizen with dual nationality. Their National Governing Body had totally different rules on eligibility from, say, those of UKA. Until the EAA gets its rules tightened and properly policed these Championships will not be held on a level playing field.

items.heading: The power of ten
items.summary: Report and Belgrave results from UK Women's Athletics League Division 2 match one at Wigan, where ten Belgrave athletes covered enough events to finish sixth.
items.text:
UK Women’s Athletics League Division 2

Match One, Wigan, 3 June 2007.

The power of ten

Only ten Belgrave athletes were able to include a trip to Wildest Wigan in their competition diaries – and the team manager’s first job was to work out how 50% of the events could be covered. Failure to do this not only means being barred from the league for the rest of the season – it means an automatic drop right through all divisions to the UKWAL qualifying match at the end of the year! But not only was this penalty avoided, the magnificent ten who were there, including Hannah Douglas who had been ill during the preceding couple of days, doubled and tripled up their performances to bring the team in 6th at the end of the match – just 2.5 points off 5th. That was some achievement.

Good points came our way in the opening track event – the 400m hurdles – where Hannah was close to her season’s best – and Jodie Favell made her Belgrave début. Sarah Gailey started her afternoon’s work with a well run 800m and Jacqui Loney and Belinda Heil began their tour of the throwing events with a high standard hammer competition. But points gained here were soon negated by the fact that we had nobody in the 100m (or later 200m) and no pole vaulters.

Michelle Nestor was our solitary long and triple jumper and she partnered Hannah in the high jump. Second and 5th places came our way in the 400m thanks to Susan Bovill, running a nifty 55.45, and Sarah Gailey. Gradually the team positions settled down with the Belles hovering in 6th or 7th spot.

The 3000m saw a 1-2 from Birhan Dagne and Sarah Murphy and when this was followed by the sprint hurdles where multi-eventers Hannah and Jodie were back in action, we gradually began to feel that a place above the relegation line might be possible.

Catherine Bryson front ran a 1500m where she built up a lead of 30m, only to be run down on the last lap so that she entered the finish straight with a Team Southampton athlete right on her shoulder. No trouble though, as Catherine had enough in hand to kick successfully for the line, and with Sarah Murphy collecting another middle-distance second place the team was now battling with Havering Mayesbrook for 5th team position. But again our lack of sprinters meant that the makeshift 4x100m quartettes were up against it and although the long relay girls fared better, we had to settle for sixth overall.

Assuming we can coax a few more athletes out for matches two and three at Eton and Rugby we should be able to hold on in division two for 2007.

items.heading: Men go through but the women are out
items.summary: Report and Belgrave results from BAL Cup round one (the new 10 in 100 format) at Copthall Stadium, Barnet, where the men won their match but the women finished last.
items.text:
BAL Cup

Round 1, Copthall Stadium, Barnet, 10 June 2007.

Men go through but the women are out

The BAL Cup entered its third and most revolutionary format this year – renamed 10 in 100 and with a minimum of eight athletes to be provided in the individual events by each team. The idea is to create a snappy meeting where the ten events plus relay are completed within 100 minutes, with men’s and women’s matches to be scored separately. Failure to provide eight athletes – even if the match is won – means no progression to the next round and therefore a late or non-arrival by a competitor could wipe out the team. Events will change to a certain extent from one round to the next but a negative point is that due to the time constraints the competition will not include a 5000m or 10000m.

Providing eight individual athletes proved to be the difficulty in round one as the Bedford International Games, BMC Nike Grand Prix and English Decathlon Championships depleted the stronger clubs. For the smaller outfits, getting athletes to come along to do just the one event, possibly not their speciality, to ensure that enough athletes made up the team was another problem. It was too much for two clubs in our own match who didn’t show up at all – but the problem was worse in a second sequence of matches held at the same venue later in the day where two competitions had to be combined to make the competition meaningful.

Matt Douglas trebled up

All this made things interesting for the team managers who had to scout around to fill out the teams. For the men’s squad a decision was taken to get Matt Douglas to treble up as he was the only available man who could hurdle and, at a pinch, high jump. Unfortunately all Matt’s events took place at the beginning of the meet – and when he wasn’t around twenty minutes before the first race, pulse rates went up a bit. But of course he made it, and after a ten-minute warm-up placed 2nd in the high hurdles, went straight to the high jump where he flopped over to gain a single height and then lined up for the 800m. Considerably less than two minutes later Matt was allowed off duty for an hour before leading out the relay team! It all made for a good training session though, and Matt was well pleased with his first 800 in 15 years which resulted in a personal record by around 10 seconds.

Sarah our first winner

But it was Sarah Gailey who provided Belgrave’s first win of the day as she tagged along behind the leader for the first lap of the women’s 800m and then went to the front along the back straight. She never quite broke away but had enough strength to ensure that nobody could get back to her. Vicky Goodwin had run in Manchester the previous night and tackled another 1500m here while Helen Arbuthnot took care of both throws, but with such a depleted team the Belles’ cup run was over early.

Set Osho tackled his first 400m of the season out of the blocks and just missed out on a win and then junior Luke Sargeant, drafted into the first team for the 200m, was delighted with his best ever time for yet another second place.

By now the javelin was coming to a conclusion and one has to applaud the courage of James Everard, due into hospital soon for yet another knee operation, who twice sent his spear over 60m and had all six throws measured well beyond the next best thrower. Halfway through the match then – and the men held a narrow lead over Blackheath & Bromley.

A final flourish clinched the match

Thirty-five year-old Kwadjo Adjepong enjoyed being pulled into the team to tackle the short sprint and he took full advantage of a wind variously reported as +5.4 and +2.4 to gain 4th spot. And then to the longest race of the day where Will Cockerell, whose racing diary recently featured the London Marathon, here gave the impression of sprinting flat out for a full 1500 metres.

Four hundred metre man Michael Peacock gamely filled in at shot putt to keep all events covered as Blackheath moved ahead in the match, but a final flourish by Richard Danso in the long jump, where Gary Wilson also excelled, and a win from the medley relay squad meant that the Bels clawed back the win.

Onwards and upwards, then, to the “semis”.

items.heading: New kid on the block
items.summary: Birth announcement of Seb, son of Dorchie and Will Cockerell.
items.text:
News … and reminiscences

New kid on the block

We welcome the arrival of young Seb who entered the arena on 31 May in the early hours of the morning, weighing in at 7½ lbs, a son to Dorchie and Will Cockerell. The young chap is said to have the legs of a runner and with parents who both own gold medals won in National Road Relays, we have every hope that Seb will be appearing in Sutton Park in due course.

items.heading: Honours Board appeal reaches its target
items.summary: Notice that the £2500 appeal to rework the team Honours Board at Belgrave Hall has reached its target.
items.text:
Honours Board appeal reaches its target

We set a target of £2500 to cover the cost of reworking our team Honours Board at Belgrave Hall. Well, thanks to the generosity of our members – and even a few non-members – that target has been reached. The revamped board is in place (and already needs a few details to be added as a result of recent achievements) and we have enough money to begin work on a second board to record the successes of our women’s teams).

Many thanks to all those who gave so generously.

items.heading: Lou goes North
items.summary: News that Louise Cooper is moving north for a new job with Cheshire Police but will still compete for Belgrave.
items.text:
Lou goes North

We’ve just heard that our recent international and stalwart of the women’s road and cross-country teams Louise Cooper is on the move. Louise tells us:

“I just thought I would let you know that I have a new job with Cheshire Police and am frantically trying to sell my house and sort everything out ready to move.

I will be really sad to leave the area, as I’ve worked for Thames Valley Police for 10 years now, and will especially miss the guys from the club too.

I still intend to compete for Belgrave up there though and will be flying the Belgrave flag in the north.”

Louise goes on to say that she is still really enjoying the ultra running scene. She has a 50k in a few weeks time and is then going for the 100k again in Holland in September.

“The last one was certainly was an experience, but looking back, I want to be stronger in the second half and not struggle as much!”

We wish Louise luck with her move and future competitions.

items.heading: Records in Loughborough International
items.summary: Belgrave performances at the Loughborough International, including Goldie Sayers' British javelin record of 65.05m.
items.text:
Records in Loughborough International

The performance of the Loughborough International meeting was Goldie Sayers’ superb javelin throw of 65.05m to beat the British Record and go top of the World Rankings for 2007. Eva Massey won the shot with a club record of 16.60m and multi-eventer Julie Hollman was victorious in the long jump and 3rd in the sprint hurdles.

For the men, Graeme Oudney was delighted with his first 800m of the year which yielded a time of 1:47.99. Stephen Sharp ran under 8:05 for 3000m, Neil Speaight was around 3:45 for 1500m and Joe Ive cleared 5.20m for 2nd in the pole vault with Keith Higham 3rd in 5.10m. Winner of the high jump was Samson Oni, clearing 2.25m.

items.heading: Kevin Sempers medals in England Athletics Decathlon
items.summary: Kevin Sempers won bronze in the England Athletics national decathlon championship with a PB of 7363 points.
items.text:
Kevin Sempers medals in England Athletics Decathlon

Kevin Sempers took the bronze medal in the England Athletics national decathlon championship with 7363 points, a PB by 106. He was second overnight with 3951, his first day best by 153 points. He sprinted 100m in 11.01 seconds, long jumped 6.95, put the shot 12.05m, won the high jump with 2.07m to equal his PB of four years ago when he was English Schools’ champion, and ended with a 400m best of 50.02 seconds yet such was the quality, he finished last in the fastest 400m heat of the day! On day two, he clocked 15.07 seconds in the 110m hurdles, threw the discus 34.12m, pole vaulted an outdoor PB 4.55m, threw the javelin 54.26m and clocked 4:53.43 in the 1500m.

items.heading: Phillips upsets the Olympic Champion
items.summary: Phillips Idowu beat Christian Olsson in the triple jump at the Bislett Games in Oslo, the first IAAF Golden League meeting of 2007.
items.text:
Phillips upsets the Olympic Champion

European Indoor triple jump champion Phillips Idowu scored a thrilling victory over the Olympic, World and European champion Christian Olsson (Sweden) at the first of this summer’s IAAF Golden League meetings, the Exxon Mobil Bislett Games in Oslo, Norway, on Friday 15 June.

Just 2cm separated the duo in their first duel of the year. Olsson took a first round lead with 17.33m to Idowu’s 17.21m. But Idowu instantly silenced those inclined to question his appetite for a high quality battle by responding with 17.35m in the second round. It proved enough for victory – though Olsson reached 17.30m with his fourth attempt.

items.heading: “Adviser” to the first four minute miler
items.summary: History of Franz Stampfl, Roger Bannister's adviser, who became Belgrave's official club coach in 1938, with extracts from the Committee minutes.
items.text:
“Adviser” to the first four minute miler

Much has been written about the race at Oxford just over fifty years ago in which Roger Bannister broke the four minute barrier for the first time. The names of the other runners in the event are, to a varying degree, known to the public. Chris Chataway won an epic race against the Russian, Kuts, at the White City, Chris Brasher took the Olympic gold medal in the 3,000 metre steeplechase in 1956. There has been a book recently about Hulatt, the fourth member of the AAAs team that night, while the other two runners, Dole and Gordon running for Oxford University, have been interviewed.

There was a Belgrave connection with the event as the photographs show – one of those supporting Bannister after the event was his “adviser” Franz Stampfl. Franz came to Britain as a refugee in the 1930s and sought help from Harold Abrahams, a barrister and senior AAAs official. Coaching for athletics was a far different proposition to that which we have today. Athletics was very much an amateur sport which makes an entry in the Club Committee minutes very interesting.

On 14th July 1938 the Honorary Secretary told the Committee that,

“upon recommendation of H M Abrahams & J C Crump of AAAs he had acquired the services of a coach to attend Battersea Park on Tuesday evenings and Sunday mornings for exclusive use of Club members. The fee would not be more than £1 per week for services of coach and Hon Sec asked that his action be endorsed. This was agreed to”.

At the next meeting it was reported that,

“With reference to the coach F L Stampfl whose services had been acquired as from 19 June Hon Sec stated that Stampfl was now going to Loughborough for 3 weeks and it was decided that a cheque covering fee of 10/- per session be sent him to date”. (sic)

So Franz Stampfl became the official Club coach. The years between 1938 and 1954 were very eventful ones and especially so for Franz. He was interned at the outbreak of war and sent to Australia. Torpedoed, rescued, then sent on board the “Dunera” to Australia. That voyage is described in a book “The Dunera Scandal” which just about says it all. Franz survived his time on board and in Australia returning to Britain in 1946, initially to Belfast, but later to Battersea where he trained many for the princely sum of one shilling a session.

A very popular, and successful man, he returned to Australia in July 1954 but not before a farewell dinner at the Savoy Grill attended by many Belgravians - and Selsonians. Frank Simmons, the Club sprint coach wrote a tribute in this magazine (May 1955 page 3).

Franz coached in Melbourne for a number of years but was involved in a car accident which left him paralysed for the rest of his life. As Frank Simmons said, he passed his experience on at a time when coaching in the UK was in its infancy and the Club’s sprinters benefited considerably from the man who “advised” Bannister before he set the record.

people.note: Belgrave official Club coach from 1938; Bannister's adviser

people.note: Club sprint coach; tribute in May 1955 Belgravian

items.heading: Moving on to the reminiscences …
items.summary: Past President Lionel Mann recalls completing 34 consecutive Maidenhead Easter 10 Miles road races between 1967 and 2000.
items.text:
Moving on to the reminiscences …

Past President Lionel Mann has recently caught up with our eBelgravian and is pleased now to be keeping up to date with all the news.

And regarding our item in the previous issue referring to the Maidenhead Easter 10 Miles Road Race – he tells us that he managed to complete 34 consecutive editions of this race between 1967 and 2000, his best time being 50:48 for 11th in 1970. Lionel’s best placing was 5th in 53:29 in 1974 at a time when the course was 10½ miles – and his worst ever was 83:15 in 2000, attributed, he says, to the “anno domino effect”.

And with Lionel owning up to a PW (personal worst) we wonder if any more of our members fancy sharing with us their personal worsts!

items.heading: Belgrave Harriers vs Birchfield Harriers in 1935
items.summary: Eric Hall's find of the 1935 British Games Jubilee Meeting programme, recalling a 3 mile match between Belgrave and Birchfield that Belgrave lost by 4 points despite Jim Ginty winning.
items.text:
Belgrave Harriers vs Birchfield Harriers in 1935

Eric Hall has come across a rather grand programme for the “News of the World” sponsored British Games Jubilee Meeting held on June 10th 1935. The occasion celebrated the Silver Jubilee of King George V and Queen Mary which meant a rather hyped up programme of events together with biographies of many of the great and the good in our sport.

An interesting item was Event 21 to be run at 3.40pm and was a 3 mile match between Belgrave and Birchfield. The note on our Club was to the effect that we were unknown before the First World War but that since then our rise had been remarkable! Our National successes had been a win in the National Cross Country that year and two wins in the London to Brighton Relay plus a number of walking titles.

Birchfield founded in 1877 are 10 years older than us and “have the most remarkable record possessed by any Club in the world”. They had won 25 National titles and 5 wins in the Brighton relay.

The Belgrave team was led by the great little man Bert Footer and his eleven Club mates included a number of characters – Arthur Allum, Tom Carter, Harry Shields, Jim Ginty, Dan Patience among them. For Birchfield Jack Webster (3 International CC caps including an individual win in 1925) captained a team including R R Sutherland (5 caps who went on to win 2 more) and Forryan (1 cap).

The Belgravian reports the race as “being long remembered by those who had the pleasure to witness it”. The team position changed frequently during the race but we lost a fine race in the last lap but only by 4 points although we had the individual winner in Jim Ginty.

The two Clubs were to go on to many other contests and, hopefully, will do so for years to come and as the Captain showed in a recent issue of the magazine close contests are the most exciting for spectators but I am not so sure if they are so enjoyed by the competitors!

Joe goes up to 5.40m

In the form of his life, 20 year-old pole-vaulter Joe Ive won the SEAA Championship at Crystal Palace with 5.30m and barely before that had sunk in, improved to 5.40m to win the England Athletics U23 title – the same height as Sale’s Paul Walker but with the Belgrave man having a superior sequence. Both unsuccessfully attempted 5.50m.

Now placed 9th equal on the European U23 list for 2007, Joe has been selected to compete in the European U23 Championships to be held in Debrecen, Hungary, in mid-July.
